author: cli
text: Handles realistic Java despite minimal test fixtures. Tested against a 150-line Spring service (@Service/@Transactional annotations, generics, lambdas, streams, nested Builder and exception classes): 16 entities and 48 edges extracted correctly, including arity-disambiguated constructors. The thin fixtures understate what the parser actually does.

author: cli
text: JAVA CALL EDGES NEVER RESOLVE TO METHODS - silent, and in the dangerous direction. Measured 2026-08-16 against google/gson (4208 entities) under 0.55.2: of 1770 resolved 'calls' edges, ZERO target a function or method; all 1770 target a class. Go/cobra is 99% and TypeScript/zod 97% on the same measurement. Consequence for a Java user: 'memway before-edit' on a method that is demonstrably called reports 'callers 0  blast 0'. Gson.newJsonWriter/1 is called at Gson.java:642 and reads 0; FieldNamingPolicy.separateCamelCase/2 is called at lines 75/97/117/144/171 and reads 0. All 3235 gson method entities are in this state. MECHANISM, and it is this project's recurring shape: add_calls emits RawEdge(scope, ntext(nm), 'calls') - the BARE method name, e.g. 'separateCamelCase' - while this parser's own overload disambiguation registers every method entity with an arity suffix, Type.method/2. 3235 of 3235 method qualnames carry '/'; 0 of 22453 emitted dst_refs do. The emitter and the registry are two representations of one name and they cannot meet. Go works because its qualnames carry no suffix, so the same bare dst_ref resolves. SECOND SYMPTOM, same root: 'memway show <repo> upperCaseFirstLetter' answers 'no entity matches' for a method that exists, because bare-name resolution compares against suffixed last segments; the closest-match list rescues the human but not the edge builder. FIX DIRECTION: resolve a bare Java target against the arity-stripped last segment, keeping the suffix as the tiebreak when arity is known at the call site (n args at the invocation) - and pin it with a real-repo recall test, because every hand-built Java fixture in the suite passes today.

author: cli
text: CORRECTION, supersedes the note below - the measurement stands, the framing was unfair. README:182 ALREADY discloses that Java is thinner: no method signatures, no doc comments, no field entities, coarser staleness. So 'memway claims Java support and does not deliver' is wrong, and I should not have implied it. Two things survive the correction, both narrower and both real. (1) The disclosed limits do not include the largest one. Nothing in that paragraph predicts that call edges never resolve to methods, so a reader who accepted every stated caveat would still expect 'who calls this method' to work. (2) AT THE POINT OF USE the briefing makes an affirmative false claim: before_edit on gson's Gson.newJsonWriter/1 returns callers 0 with downstream.is_lower_bound FALSE and warnings []. The grounding block does hedge - '1 edge(s) in this radius are guesses ... verify before trusting the counts' - so the tool is not silently confident, which is what I first said. But is_lower_bound is THE field this project uses to say 'there may be more than I can see', and it is wired at query.py:513 to exactly one cause, radius_is_lower_bound from dynamic event emission. A whole language's unresolvable call targets do not reach it. CHEAP HONEST FIX, independent of fixing Java resolution and worth doing first: if any raw call edge's dst_ref matches this entity's arity-stripped name but failed to resolve, the caller list IS a lower bound - say so and warn. That is language-agnostic, computable from data already on disk, and converts a false 0 into an honest 'at least 0'.

author: cli
text: FIXED in 0.56.0 - supersedes both notes below, which diagnosed it and then corrected the framing. add_calls now emits refs.render(name, arity=<argument count at the call site>), and the declaration registers through the same producer, so the two spellings are one. Re-measured on google/gson at the same clone: resolved call edges 1770 -> 4919, of which 3150 are method -> method where there were ZERO; the remaining 1769 method -> class are constructor calls and correctly target types. Gson.newJsonWriter/1 reads callers 7, blast 34 where it read 0 and 0, and is_lower_bound correctly drops to False because there is nothing unresolved left to admit. The narrower survivor of the correction also holds: README:182 still describes Java as thinner (no signatures, no doc comments, no field entities) and this release does not change that - it fixes resolution, not coverage.
